rationale_summary: NIST IR 8596 (Cyber AI Profile) is dominantly framed around consumer_public_safety, centering on operational system resilience and protecting organizations, infrastructure (such as power grids and OT/ICS), and users from AI-related failures, data leakage, poisoning, prompt injection, deepfake phishing, and AI-accelerated cyberattacks. Consumer_public_safety narrowly edges out innovation_enablement, which is a strong runner-up emphasizing adaptable, voluntary, technology-neutral guidance that enables organizations to strategically adopt AI and capitalize on AI-enabled cyber defense efficiencies. National_security serves as a clear third frame through explicit attention to advanced persistent threats (APTs), offensive cyber operations, autonomous attack agents, AI-orchestrated espionage, and critical infrastructure resilience, with minor supporting roles for economic welfare, privacy/civil liberties compliance, and machine-speed autonomous cyber risks.
